title: MacNeal–Harder twisted beam
source: MacNeal and Harder, 'A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy', Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1 (1985) 3–20, Fig. 6 (p. 8), Table 3 (p. 10)

quantities.quantity: tip displacement along the in-plane load (width direction, u_z at the tip centre)
quantities.reason: MacNeal and Harder grade an element A within 2% of the theoretical value on the prescribed coarse mesh (p. 14); the 12 × 2 mesh gives 1.022 and 0.960 of the theory, recorded as a known failure with its two causes (README)
quantities.known_failure: 1.022 of the theory at 12 × 2 (1.028, 1.031 and 1.032 at 24 × 4, 48 × 8 and 96 × 16): the drilling penalty γ = G/100 lets the rotation about the normal lag the membrane's on the twisted surface, which adds (t τ)² / (6 (1 − ν) γ/G) = 3.75% to the plate-bending compliance at any mesh (issue #1077)

quantities.quantity: tip displacement along the out-of-plane load (normal direction, u_y at the tip centre)
quantities.reason: MacNeal and Harder grade an element A within 2% of the theoretical value on the prescribed coarse mesh (p. 14); the 12 × 2 mesh gives 1.022 and 0.960 of the theory, recorded as a known failure with its two causes (README)
quantities.known_failure: 0.960 of the theory at 12 × 2 (1.005, 1.020 and 1.024 at 24 × 4, 48 × 8 and 96 × 16): the bilinear membrane's parasitic shear in in-plane bending (estimated at about −6.5% at this element length, gone with refinement along the span) against the same drilling softness as in_plane (issue #1077)
